# Historical evidence synthesis: textual-kitty-key-phases

## Scope and coverage

This batch contains **one student source file and one recorded attempt**, H0007, covered by five supplied chunk audit reports. The reports describe model-reviewed chunks of the same trajectory, not five independent trials. The inventory counts 276 units, 275 events and 96 tool events. The original task prompt is not visible in the reports, so the goal below is reconstructed from the student’s work, not treated as a complete specification. The underlying patch and formal evaluation output were not independently inspected for this synthesis.

All event citations refer to **H0007**, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-baseline-run/runs/baseline_ds1017_textual_a1_vm8_20261120_r1/infer_logs/textual-kitty-key-phases/turn_1/trajs.json`. Inventory-reported artifacts are the adjacent `patch.diff` and `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-baseline-run/runs/baseline_ds1017_textual_a1_vm8_20261120_r1/eval_output/textual-kitty-key-phases/eval_result.json`.

## Evidence matrix

| Dimension | Evidence | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Goal and baseline | The student described Kitty key phases, modifiers, alternate keys, text and legacy fallbacks (main_agent events 34, 39, 68). Baseline probes showed extended sequences emitted as individual characters and observed Alt-prefix loss for legacy control keys (111–112). | Task interpretation and baseline behavior are evidenced; the full original specification is not. |
| Stops and constraints | Git-ref and unreachable-object searches were denied by hooks directing local investigation (30, 32, 69–70). A sleep command was separately blocked (227). | Permission/operational stops, not algorithmic failures. No branch or CLI stop is established. |
| Executed update | Successful edits added key metadata and extended parsing (114–130); a probe exposed an unexpected `shift+A` result and the student corrected the text branch (133–136). Alias-binding edits were confirmed (145, 148, 150); further text handling edits followed (191, 197). A four-file change was committed (266–267). | Actual implementation, not merely advice or an empty patch. Inventory reports a 17,870-byte patch. |
| Targeted validation | Probes and assertions passed, including a shifted-alias binding check; four targeted test files reported 89 passed and 1 xfailed (155–164, 199–200, 256–257, 269–270). | Direct evidence for exercised cases, not comprehensive correctness. |
| Broader validation | One broad run was stopped after timing out to background (187–188, 194, 205–206). Another was interrupted with 362 passed, 2 failed and 1 xfailed (245). Both TextArea failures were reproduced in a clean HEAD worktree (245–251). | Interrupted runs are not full passes. The clean comparison weakens patch-regression attribution for those two failures but does not identify their cause. |
| Formal outcome | Inventory reports **solved**, 23/23 fail-to-pass and 57/57 pass-to-pass, and `end_turn`. | Recorded formal success; the underlying evaluation trace is not visible in the supplied reports. |
| Teacher and Scene | A system-prompt archive is linked, but its contents are not supplied; the reports identify no delivered teacher text or adoption. This is a code task, with no scene or image evidence. | Advice availability is not receipt. Teacher diagnosis, executed advice-driven update, validation of such advice and independent quality attributable to it are unestablished. Scene-specific receipt, acceptance and visual-quality questions are not applicable. |

## Comparison and interpretation

The record contains one overall attempt, not separate successful and failed solution trials. Its **reported formal success** and successful targeted tests coexist with a **partial, interrupted broader run** containing two failures. Those failures were reproduced against a clean baseline, so they should neither be attributed to the patch as established regressions nor ignored as passes. The earlier unexpected `shift+A` probe is a visible intermediate behavioral mismatch followed by an executed correction, rather than evidence that the final attempt failed. Conversely, denied searches and the blocked sleep command are operational constraints, not observations of faulty keyboard behavior.

The student explored local parser, dispatch and binding paths after the search denials. The most transferable observations are evidentiary: confirm edits and their call sites separately; distinguish targeted checks from incomplete broad runs; and compare suspected regressions with a clean baseline without treating that comparison as a root-cause diagnosis. Here, the alias helper and its call-site edits have separate confirmation (145, 148, 150), while the baseline comparison concerns only the two observed TextArea failures (245–251).

Kitty sequence fields, shifted aliases, associated text and legacy escape handling are **task-specific**. For example, the observed ESC+DEL mapping to `ctrl+w` and ESC+backspace mapping to `alt+backspace` (169–173) are compatibility facts in this record, not general rules for all terminals. Unverified hypotheses remain about untested sequences, binding paths and the cause of the TextArea failures. The formal score and targeted passes do not resolve all of them.

No teacher-delivered guidance is evidenced across the supplied chunk reports. The linked archive establishes availability only; it cannot establish what the student received, diagnosed, adopted or validated. Similarly, no independent scene-quality assessment applies. This absence is not proof that no teacher input existed outside the reported evidence. Model-call usage and cost fields are blank: usage is not established, and historical cost cannot be recovered from that absence.
